faq.a: Salman is associated with the Arabic form سَلْمَان, whose core sense is salman; safe, sound.

faq.q: What is the origin of Salman?
faq.a: Salman is associated with Arabic. Salman is Arabic سَلْمَان (Salmān), associated with the sense 'safe, sound'. It was borne by a well-known companion of the Prophet.
Yes — the underlying form سَلْمَان is Arabic.
Salman can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Salman should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Salmān is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Salman mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Salman is rendered سلمان and carries the sense سلمان، محفوظ.

faq.q: What does Salman mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Salman is rendered سلمان and carries the sense سلمان، بی‌گزند.
A romanized syllable approximation is sal-man. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Salman?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Salman, salman. Script forms are سلمان, سَلْمَان, सलमान.

faq.q: Is Salman a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
